entities.summary: Erasistratus was a Greek anatomist and royal physician under Seleucus I Nicator of Syria. Along with fellow physician Herophilus, he founded a school of anatomy in Alexandria, where they carried out anatomical research. As well, he is credited with helping to found the methodic school of teachings of medicine in Alexandria whilst opposing traditional humoral theories of Hippocratic ideologies. Together with Herophilus, he is credited by historians as the potential founder of neuroscience due to his acknowledgements of nerves and their roles in motor control through the brain and skeletal muscles.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Erasistratus' contributions to anatomy and his opposition to traditional humoral theories laid groundwork for the methodic school of medicine in Alexandria, influencing subsequent medical thought and practice. His work as a royal physician under Seleucus I Nicator also highlights the intersection of science and politics during the Hellenistic period.
